entries.title: Benjamini-Schramm spectral criterion with explicit normalization
entries.statement: KNOWN SUFFICIENT CRITERION; source audit pending. For independent Bernoulli bond percolation on an infinite connected d-regular simple Cayley graph G, write rho=||A_G||/d for simple random walk. If d*rho*p_c(G)<1, then p_c(G)<p_u(G). The condition is sufficient and cannot be inferred from nonamenability alone for the prescribed generators.
assumptions: Infinite connected locally finite d-regular simple Cayley graph
rho is the normalized simple-random-walk spectral radius

entries.title: False universal spectral bridge for prescribed Cayley generators
entries.statement: FALSE AUXILIARY CLAIM, recorded for refutation: every infinite connected nonamenable d-regular simple Cayley graph with independent Bernoulli bond percolation satisfies d*rho*p_c<1, where rho=||A||/d. This is stronger than the nonuniqueness conjecture and fails on the explicitly specified simple C_2*C_3 graph.
assumptions: This entry records a false proposed bridge, not an accepted theorem

entries.title: Simple C_2*C_3 triangle-block boundary and spectral obstruction
entries.statement: DRAFT AUTHOR PROOF; independent review pending; no novelty claim. Let G be the simple undirected Cayley graph of <a,b | a^2=b^3=1> with the symmetric generating set {a,b,b^-1}. Each unordered a-edge appears once. In iid Bernoulli bond percolation, p_c=q, the unique root in (0,1) of 2q^2+2q^3-2q^4=1, with 0.63<q<0.64, and p_u=1. No infinite cluster exists at p<=q; for each fixed q<p<1 there are almost surely infinitely many; at p=1 there is one. The edge Cheeger constant is 1/3. For rho=||A||/3, the triangle Rayleigh bound gives 3*rho*p_c>=2q>1.26. This refutes universal satisfaction of the sufficient spectral criterion while proving this special case of nonuniqueness.
assumptions: Simple undirected graph: one a-edge, not two parallel a-bonds

entries.title: C0047-A001 source normalization correction
entries.statement: AUDIT CORRECTION (w559, 2026-10-10; independent review pending) of the 2026-09-07 C0047-A001 spectral route. For independent Bernoulli bond percolation on an infinite connected d-regular simple Cayley graph G, let rho=||A_G||/d denote the normalized simple-random-walk spectral radius. Benjamini-Schramm 1996, Theorem 4, printed p.76 (bond extension in section 2), and Juschenko-Nagnibeda 2015, Theorem 2, give the sufficient condition d*rho*p_c(G)<1 for p_c(G)<p_u(G). The original p_c<1/rho quotation omitted d and is not that criterion: it is automatic when rho<1 and p_c<=1. Nonamenability does not imply the repaired criterion for a prescribed generating set. In the simple Cayley graph C_2*C_3 with generators {a,b,b^-1}, p_c=q is the root of 2q^2+2q^3-2q^4=1 in (0.63,0.64), p_u=1, and ||A||>=2, so d*rho*p_c>1.26. This counterexample refutes only the stronger universal spectral bridge. An existence theorem for a favorable generating multiset does not establish the result for every prescribed simple generating set. The parent conjecture is not solved by this packet; current 2026 openness is UNKNOWN because a recent public full-result claim has not received a mathematical or comparator proof check here.
assumptions: A correction to the unreviewed 2026-09-07 attempt record
No full-conjecture solution or current-openness certification

entries.title: Order-two Cayley edge multiplicity changes bond thresholds
entries.statement: DRAFT AUTHOR MODEL CHECK; independent review pending. In the simple C_2*C_3 triangle graph with one a-edge per unordered pair, the forward branching mean is 2p^2+2p^3-2p^4. Replacing every a-edge by two independent parallel Bernoulli(p) bonds changes its connection probability to 2p-p^2 and the branching mean to 4p^2+2p^3-6p^4+2p^5. Its critical equation is 2p^5-6p^4+2p^3+4p^2-1=0, with root in (0.51,0.53), rather than the simple-graph root in (0.63,0.64). These polynomials are checked by 32 and 128 exact local configurations respectively. Kozakova 2008 reports the latter polynomial with Cayley edge multiplicity; that published number must not be transplanted into the simple graph at the same p.
assumptions: Independent bond model, not site percolation
Parallel bonds are distinct random variables
Published-model interpretation is identified as an inference in MODEL_CONVENTIONS.md
